cases.statement: One affected carrier described in a primary report: P3 of PMID 36325013, a 3-year-old girl with SLE and lupus nephritis class IV, heterozygous, inherited from her asymptomatic mother. The review 39125844 (Table 2 row 33) and the Chinese-language paper 41905891 (its reference [9]) both summarise this same girl from PMID 36325013; the pipeline merged the 39125844 row (HA20-ID0222) but gave the 41905891 row a separate identity (HA20-ID0764).

people.key_phenotypes: SLE with lupus nephritis class IV from age 3; autoimmune haemolytic anaemia; intermittent fever; frequent oral ulcers; hepatosplenomegaly and lymphadenopathy

quotes.quote: P3 was a 3-year-old girl born at term with low birthweight.

She was diagnosed with SLE because of intermittent fever, frequent oral ulcers, hyperaemic rash on both palms, haemolytic anaemia, proteinuria, haematuria, decreased C3 and C4 and multiple positive autoantibodies (Table 3).
Additionally, she had hepatosplenomegaly and multiple swollen lymph nodes.

phenotype_specificity.statement: The authors note that their patients were predominantly autoimmune (lupus nephritis) rather than the classic autoinflammatory HA20 picture, while sharing features such as oral ulcers, fever and hepatosplenomegaly. Trio WES was performed for P3. WES also found common SLE risk alleles in P3, including NCF2 p.R314W (Table 5).

quotes.quote: For patient 2 (P2) and patient 3 (P3), WES was performed and analysed concurrently for the proband and both parents.
In contrast, our patients were predominantly characterized by autoimmune features with LN.
However, two patients (P2 and P3) showed marked autoimmunity at a very early age (<3 year) and P3 showed obvious autoimmune characteristics from the onset.

segregation.statement: One unaffected carrier: the mother carries the variant and is asymptomatic (confirmed by Sanger sequencing). No affected relative carrying the variant is reported. The father was sequenced in the trio but his result is not stated in the text.

quotes.quote: Her asymptomatic mother had the same mutation confirmed by Sanger sequencing (Fig. 3C and D).
Additionally, P3’s mother had a corresponding mutation but is still asymptomatic, suggesting a significant degree of variable expressivity and reduced penetrance in HA20 patients.
患儿母亲携带相同变异，但无临床症状

de_novo.statement: Not de novo: inherited from the asymptomatic mother.

quotes.quote: | Mutation origin | From mother | De novo | From mother |

functional.statement: No assay of this variant is reported. RNA-seq and qPCR were done on P1 only. Serum IL-6 was measured in all three patients (raised versus six controls); this is a patient biomarker, not a test of the variant.

quotes.quote: (I) Elevated serum cytokine IL-6 levels in the three patients (controls = 6).

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Two-nucleotide substitution (delins) creating a stop codon, p.(Ala434Ter) per the batch HGVS (agrees with the paper's p.A434*). The authors presume it causes A20 haploinsufficiency and state it removes zinc fingers 2-7.

quotes.quote: This mutation caused a premature stop codon directly and was presumed to result in A20 haploinsufficiency.
The third mutation, c.1300_1301delinsTA (p. A434*), results in a premature stop codon that removes zinc finger domains 2–7.

population_data_in_papers.statement: Stated absent from gnomAD, ChinaMAP, in-house controls and Infevers.

quotes.quote: All novel mutations were absent from gnomAD, ChinaMAP [14] Chinese Millionome database, in-house controls and Infevers (an online database for auto-inflammatory mutations; https://infevers.umai-montpellier.fr/web).

authors_classification.statement: The authors call the three variants, including this one, novel pathogenic and loss-of-function mutations. No ACMG criteria are stated.

quotes.quote: In summary, we report the clinical manifestations and immunological characteristics of three biopsy-proven LN patients with novel pathogenic mutations in the TNFAIP3 gene.
Novel loss-of-function mutations in TNFAIP3 gene in patients with lupus nephritis

concerns: Same-person duplicate: HA20-ID0764 (41905891, 'ref [9] patient') is the same girl as HA20-ID0222 (P3 of 36325013). 41905891 cites its ref [9] as PMID 36325013 and repeats the same age at onset (3 years), sex, features and asymptomatic carrier mother. Count her once.

39125844 (review) is also a secondary summary of P3, not an independent case. It marks family history 'Positive' and says 'Her family history seemed to be positive', while the primary paper says the carrier mother is asymptomatic. Elsewhere it attributes p.Ala434Ter to its ref [69] (a different paper, Alhebshi 2020); the table row cites [30] (PMID 36325013).
Carrier not in the batch: P3's asymptomatic mother (heterozygous by Sanger).
Other variants in the same person: WES Table 5 lists common SLE risk alleles in P3, including NCF2 p.R314W, CDKN1B, IFIH1 p.A946T and SLC29A3 p.V239I.
Transcript not stated in any paper; the batch uses NM_001270508.2.
notes_for_panel: One proband, three reports. The only family data is one asymptomatic carrier mother, which the authors themselves read as reduced penetrance. No variant-specific functional assay.
